title: Correlated grid control and loss of essential power
summary: Could a shared control error outrun grid protection and essential-service recovery?

roleTypes.label: Enabling condition
roleTypes.definition: A circumstance makes a route possible. It does not by itself establish a hazard.

roleTypes.label: Unsafe control action
roleTypes.definition: An action or omission linked to its controller, hazardous context, and affected constraint.

roleTypes.label: Loss scenario
roleTypes.definition: An explanation of how control can become inadequate, including feedback and execution problems.

roleTypes.label: Hazardous state
roleTypes.definition: A system state that can produce a loss together with relevant environmental conditions.

roleTypes.label: Optional amplifier
roleTypes.definition: A factor that could strengthen a route but is not required in every version.

roleTypes.label: Loss
roleTypes.definition: An outcome stakeholders seek to prevent, kept distinct from its contributing causes.

roleTypes.label: Recovery
roleTypes.definition: A response re-establishes enforceable safety constraints within a specified boundary. Its success requires verification.

limitingConditions.example: Independently enforced review, access bounds, or effective interruption.
limitingConditions.question: Which specified mechanism blocks the transition, and what demonstrates that it works?

limitingConditions.example: The system cannot perform the required research, deception, or physical task.
limitingConditions.question: Would increased capability remove this limit?

limitingConditions.example: The necessary access, resources, or institutional delegation is unavailable.
limitingConditions.question: Can the system or another actor acquire what is missing?

limitingConditions.example: Activity ends for a reason that does not establish an effective safeguard.
limitingConditions.question: What actually ended the episode, and would that circumstance recur?

schema: Selected losses, hazards, control relationships, contextual unsafe actions, and loss scenarios are traced to constraints. Numbered milestones summarize this analysis. They are not STPA steps. Incident evidence and hypothetical continuations remain distinct.
limits: This is a bounded first-pass analysis, not an exhaustive STPA or a completed CAST investigation. Selected actions illustrate the four unsafe-action categories. Domain experts must examine every relevant action and context. No probabilities, barrier independence, or comparative distance to catastrophe are inferred. Barrier condition describes the stated observation, not a prediction about a more capable AI.
scope: The hypothetical scenario concerns a regional electricity system using related AI forecasts or control recommendations. It includes model procurement, dispatch authorization, physical protection, regional coordination, and restoration. Essential services enter the analysis through their dependence on electricity and backup capacity.
purpose: Keep electricity within safe operating limits and maintain essential services during disturbances, preventing prolonged outages, serious illness, and loss of life.
boundary: Functional roles describe an analytical system, not the organization chart of a particular utility. Historical blackouts test physical-control assumptions only. They are not AI incidents and do not validate the proposed AI initiating mechanism.
numbering: 0 gives the context. 1.x identifies precursors, 2.x the loss-of-control event, and 3.x conditional consequences. R identifies a possible recovery outcome. These numbers locate scenario components. They are not STPA method steps or a measure of proximity to catastrophe. Both incident overlays are non-AI comparisons. Neither establishes progression through the AI-related precursors.
bowtie: The centre is H1: grid instability exceeds available containment and interrupts regional supply. Prevention acts before this state. Restoration and essential-service support can still prevent a public-health catastrophe. All right-hand transitions require additional conditions.

losses.title: Prolonged loss of essential electricity
losses.text: People and organizations lose dependable power for care, water, temperature control, and other essential activity.

losses.title: Excess illness and deaths
losses.text: Affected populations suffer substantial avoidable illness and mortality when essential-service interruption exceeds their capacity to cope.

hazards.title: Instability escapes effective containment
hazards.text: The electricity system operates outside enforceable stability limits and cannot arrest a disturbance before regional supply is interrupted.

hazards.title: Consequential dispatch exceeds the assured envelope
hazards.text: Correlated recommendations influence actual control without adequate independent checks against the current regional physical state.

hazards.title: Essential-service recovery cannot bridge the outage
hazards.text: Restoration, backup power, or support arrives too late to sustain essential services through the interruption.

controllers.title: Planning and deployment authority
controllers.responsibility: Authorize model use, establish operating envelopes, and require independent contingency validation.
controllers.feedback: Joint-system studies, model changes, protection settings, and evidence of correlated failures.
controllers.assumption: Different model names do not establish independent data, objectives, or failure modes.

controllers.title: Grid operator and regional coordinator
controllers.responsibility: Authorize dispatch, keep reserves, coordinate neighboring systems, and initiate corrective action.
controllers.feedback: Current topology, flows, voltage, reserve availability, tool health, and confirmed execution.
controllers.assumption: An unalarmed display is not evidence of a secure physical system.

controllers.title: AI forecast and recommendation service
controllers.responsibility: Provide bounded recommendations, uncertainty, and versioned inputs within an approved operating role.
controllers.feedback: Measurements, authorization limits, and validation results.
controllers.assumption: A high average forecast score does not establish safe joint behavior during unusual conditions.

controllers.title: Grid actuation and protection systems
controllers.responsibility: Execute dispatch and protection actions within coordinated physical limits and report actual state.
controllers.feedback: Local electrical measurements, device status, and operator commands.
controllers.assumption: A device protecting itself can still interact unsafely with regional protection.

controllers.title: Restoration and essential-service operators
controllers.responsibility: Restore supply, activate tested backup, and coordinate essential loads and public-health support.
controllers.feedback: Energized-load verification, available power, fuel, communications, and unmet essential needs.
controllers.assumption: Restored bulk supply and restored service at a hospital or water facility are different observations.

controlLoops.action: Approve deployment / constrain or suspend recommendations
controlLoops.feedback: C3 supplies changes. Independent studies report correlated behavior and coverage gaps.

controlLoops.action: Approve dispatch / reserve / emergency corrective action
controlLoops.feedback: C4 returns physical state and action confirmation through independently checked measurements.

controlLoops.action: Approve coordinated protection settings and operating envelope
controlLoops.feedback: Joint studies and disturbance records show interactions across regional facilities.

controlLoops.action: Sequence restoration and prioritize essential load
controlLoops.feedback: C5 reports actual restoration, available support, and remaining unmet needs.

constraints.title: Independent dispatch limits
constraints.text: AI recommendations must influence dispatch only inside a physical envelope checked independently of their shared assumptions.
constraints.test: Can related models produce individually plausible commands that violate a regional limit when executed together?
constraints.limit: Shared inputs, missing external facilities, or objectives that use up reserve margins can undermine independent dispatch checks.

improvement.title: Check the combined physical effect
improvement.proposal: Place an independently maintained operating-envelope check between AI dispatch recommendations and authorization. Evaluate their combined effect on the network rather than approving each recommendation in isolation.
improvement.test: In a validated simulator, submit individually acceptable recommendations that become unsafe together. Check whether the independent limit blocks their joint authorization.
improvement.remaining: An inaccurate network model or a shared bad input could mislead both the recommendation and its check.

constraints.title: Coordinated physical protection
constraints.text: Operating limits and protection actions must account for their joint effects across the affected network.
constraints.test: Do independent network simulations and staged drills contain the specified credible combinations of disturbances?
constraints.limit: Unmodeled neighboring systems, stale topology, conflicting relay behavior, or inadequate reserves can defeat coordinated protection.

improvement.title: Review protection across the boundary
improvement.proposal: Require neighboring operators to review joint protection settings against a shared, current network model. Resolve incompatible assumptions before approving a material operating change.
improvement.test: Use a validated simulator to carry a disturbance across an operator boundary. Check whether the agreed protection limits contain it without relying on unavailable reserves.
improvement.remaining: Stale topology or an unmodeled interaction could still defeat the coordinated protection.

constraints.title: Trusted state and timely corrective action
constraints.text: Operators must know when situational awareness is impaired and act within the remaining intervention window.
constraints.test: Does loss or staleness of a monitoring tool trigger a verified fallback and timely corrective decision?
constraints.limit: Common telemetry failures, undetected backup failure, and coordination delay can prevent timely corrective action.

improvement.title: Make loss of visibility visible
improvement.proposal: Show operators when the primary state estimate or alarm service becomes unreliable. Provide independently maintained fallback measurements with a rehearsed route to corrective action.
improvement.test: In a safe drill, disable the primary monitoring path. Check whether operators recognize the loss of visibility and act using the fallback evidence in time.
improvement.remaining: The fallback may share the same failed input, communications link, or power dependency.

constraints.title: Verified restoration capability
constraints.text: Restoration plans must reach essential loads under the actual outage conditions and verify sustained service before normal operation resumes.
constraints.test: Can restoration work when a neighboring supply, telecommunications service, or usual recovery tool is unavailable?
constraints.limit: Shared regional dependencies, inaccessible equipment, and early restart can undermine restoration.

improvement.title: Rehearse restoration without the usual help
improvement.proposal: Exercise restoration under a scenario in which the usual neighboring supply or coordination service is unavailable. Confirm that essential loads can be supported before relying on the restoration plan.
improvement.test: Use a validated exercise to withhold that support. Measure time to essential-load service and whether the restored supply can be sustained.
improvement.remaining: A longer or wider disruption could exhaust the resources available for restoration.

constraints.title: Essential services outlast interruption
constraints.text: Backup and public-health support must cover essential needs until dependable service is restored.
constraints.test: Can care, water, and safe temperatures be sustained for the specified outage duration, including fuel delivery and staffing?
constraints.limit: Fuel, water, communications, and staff may depend on the same electricity system.

improvement.title: Check the dependencies behind backup power
improvement.proposal: Make essential-service continuity planning account for the fuel and support services needed to sustain backup power. Assign responsibility for each dependency that could fail during the same outage.
improvement.test: Run a tabletop exercise in which a key resupply route is unavailable. Check how long the essential service can actually continue and when protective alternatives must begin.
improvement.remaining: A prolonged regional outage could interrupt several dependencies at once, exceeding the tested endurance.

nodes.title: Related models shape dispatch
nodes.text: Operators rely widely on related AI recommendations while keeping tight operating margins.
nodes.requires: Shared error modes, consequential authority, and insufficient independent margin.
nodes.mechanism: Delegation creates a potential common failure route. Widespread AI use alone does not establish unsafe dispatch.

nodes.title: A shared error reaches the grid
nodes.shortLabel: A shared error reaches the grid
nodes.text: Erroneous recommendations are accepted into consequential dispatch or control.
nodes.requires: An unusual condition, correlated error, and authorization outside the safe envelope.
nodes.mechanism: Independent physical checks must fail or be bypassed before recommendation error becomes a hazardous command.

nodes.title: Instability defeats containment
nodes.text: Limits, reserves, and protection fail to contain the disturbance, interrupting regional supply.
nodes.requires: A destabilizing disturbance and insufficient or counterproductive coordinated response.
nodes.mechanism: This is the control-loss threshold. A widespread outage need not continue into failed restoration or mortality.

nodes.title: Essential services outlast backup
nodes.text: The outage lasts longer than restoration and backup can sustain essential services.
nodes.requires: Sufficient outage duration, exposed essential loads, and unavailable substitutes.
nodes.mechanism: Cross-sector dependencies can defeat restoration and backup together. Their independence must be tested.

nodes.title: Illness and deaths increase
nodes.text: Loss of care, water, or safe temperatures causes excess illness and deaths.
nodes.requires: Vulnerable people are exposed long enough, and effective support remains unavailable.
nodes.mechanism: Mortality requires a separate exposure and public-health analysis. Neither mapped incident provides an AI-related mortality estimate.

nodes.title: Supply and essential care restored
nodes.text: Restoration and support re-establish sustained service within the affected area.
nodes.requires: Available sources, safe switching, coordination, and verification at essential loads.
nodes.mechanism: Successful recovery may limit duration and further harm even after prevention has failed.

links.label: Restoration and backup cannot bridge the outage
Restoration succeeds and essential service is verified

unsafeActions.action: Authorizes dispatch based on a shared erroneous recommendation
unsafeActions.context: The combined command violates the current regional safety envelope or consumes needed reserves.

unsafeActions.action: Does not initiate a required corrective action
unsafeActions.context: A disturbance or loss of trustworthy state information requires action before regional stability is lost.

unsafeActions.action: Restores loads before the supplying network can sustain them
unsafeActions.context: The switching sequence or available generation cannot safely accept the planned load.

unsafeActions.action: Ends emergency supply coordination too soon
unsafeActions.context: Essential loads still lack dependable electricity or a viable backup handover.

scenarios.title: A shared model assumption becomes a shared physical command
scenarios.archetype: Unsafe controller behavior / inadequate process model
scenarios.text: Related models underrepresent a rare condition. The operator accepts mutually compatible-looking recommendations, while independent checks share the missing assumption or fail to consider joint execution.
scenarios.unknown: The deployed models, common inputs, permitted authority, and actual correlation of consequential errors remain unspecified.

scenarios.title: The display and the physical grid diverge
scenarios.text: The operator loses a trustworthy picture of topology or reserve state. Missing or late cross-boundary information prevents the right corrective action before the intervention window closes.
scenarios.unknown: The analysis has not established which measurements remain independent, when the loss of awareness becomes visible, or what action remains feasible.

scenarios.title: Protective devices interact unsafely
scenarios.text: A correctly commanded local action interacts with neighboring protection or power flows in an unanticipated way. Device-level success can coexist with regional containment failure.
scenarios.unknown: The physical response, protection timing, and modeled boundary of every relevant scheme still need to be established.

scenarios.title: Shared dependencies exhaust the recovery window
scenarios.text: Restoration and backup rely on unavailable regional inputs. Premature reconnection or withdrawal of emergency support prolongs exposure. Substantial health loss additionally requires vulnerable populations and inadequate substitutes.
scenarios.unknown: The analysis has not established outage duration, essential-load coverage, backup endurance, public-health exposure, or counterfactual mortality.

passages.title: Restoration worked with available power
passages.locator: Executive summary, printed p. 3; PDF page 5
passages.text: FERC/NERC reports restoration of all affected load or customers in roughly 6–12 hours. Available power from the entities or their neighbors meant black-start plans were not used; some communication and coordination delays occurred.
passages.scope: This passage describes historical recovery from a non-AI event. Restoration of load does not establish uninterrupted essential services, recovery without neighboring supply, or an absence of health harm.

targets.label: Grid safeguards can fail before restoration takes effect

assessments.scope: This case provides a comparison for physical grid control and recovery. It does not establish an AI initiating error, universal backup failure, or mortality.

trace.text: One line tripped in a system not securely prepared for that contingency.
Overloads and protective actions spread the disturbance.
Utilities restored load over hours using available neighboring power.

barriers.title: Regional contingency planning
barriers.action: Use planning and operating limits to contain credible disturbances.
barriers.efficacy: FERC/NERC found planning and situational-awareness deficiencies.
barriers.durability: The safety boundary must include relevant neighboring facilities and protection interactions.
barriers.failure: A local model omits a regional interaction and authorizes an insecure state.

view.failureRoute: A local model omits a regional interaction and authorizes an insecure state.

dependencies.label: Regional model coverage
dependencies.assessment: The safety boundary must include relevant neighboring facilities and protection interactions.

reinforcement.label: Proposed improvement
reinforcement.proposal: Review joint protection and operating limits independently.
reinforcement.test: Test the modeled disturbance across the complete affected network.
reinforcement.basis: This is an analytical proposal. Its effectiveness is unassessed.

barriers.title: Restoration with available power
barriers.action: Re-energize the affected system using available internal or neighboring supply.
barriers.efficacy: The report records completed load restoration. See the linked recovery passage.
barriers.durability: This recovery depended on available power and coordination. It did not test a region-wide loss of all starting sources.
barriers.failure: The same disruption removes recovery sources, communications, or safe switching capability.

view.failureRoute: The same disruption removes recovery sources, communications, or safe switching capability.

dependencies.label: Available recovery power
dependencies.assessment: This recovery depended on available power and coordination. It did not test a region-wide loss of all starting sources.

reinforcement.label: Proposed improvement
reinforcement.proposal: Exercise restoration when the usual neighboring source is absent.
reinforcement.test: Verify essential-load service and restoration time in that adverse scenario.
reinforcement.basis: This is an analytical proposal. Its effectiveness is unassessed.

reach.local: A line loss triggered cascading outages. FERC/NERC identified inadequate planning and situational awareness. Recovery was generally effective but took hours and essential services were disrupted.
reach.systemic: This case provides a comparison for physical grid control and recovery. It does not establish an AI initiating error, universal backup failure, or mortality.

targets.label: Operational safeguards failed to contain a grid disturbance

assessments.scope: This case provides a comparison for grid limits, monitoring, and containment. It does not attribute the initiating conditions to AI.

trace.text: Planning and operating criteria did not adequately reflect vulnerabilities.
Monitoring, backup tools, and communication were inadequate.
The findings connect these weaknesses to the blackout.

barriers.title: Monitoring and backup awareness
barriers.action: Provide operators with a reliable picture of changing grid conditions and tool health.
barriers.efficacy: The task force identified ineffective monitoring, backup tools, and regional diagnostic support.
barriers.durability: A backup is useful only if its failure modes and state information are sufficiently independent.
barriers.failure: Operators continue without a reliable view of the hazardous state.

view.failureRoute: Operators continue without a reliable view of the hazardous state.

dependencies.label: Independent feedback
dependencies.assessment: A backup is useful only if its failure modes and state information are sufficiently independent.

reinforcement.label: Proposed improvement
reinforcement.proposal: Provide explicit tool-health warnings and independent fallback measurements.
reinforcement.test: Disable the primary monitoring path in a drill and verify timely operator recovery.
reinforcement.basis: This is an analytical proposal. Its effectiveness is unassessed.

reach.local: The task force identified inadequate voltage criteria, ineffective monitoring and backup tools, vegetation management failures, and deficient regional diagnostic support.
reach.systemic: This case provides a comparison for grid limits, monitoring, and containment. It does not attribute the initiating conditions to AI.

conditions.S-01:2: Only if correlated error reaches actual control
conditions.S-01:4: If outage duration exceeds recovery and backup

SW-2011.title: Southwest blackout · 2011
SW-2011.observed: A disturbance cascaded across the regional grid. Operators restored supply using power that remained available.
SW-2011.notEstablished: The event does not establish an AI initiating error or show that every backup failed. It does not establish excess deaths from the outage.
SW-2011.limit: The blackout provides a comparison for physical containment and restoration. It does not establish an AI initiating event or the hypothetical mortality branch.

regional-contingency-limits.title: Contingency limits
regional-contingency-limits.conditionBasis: The investigation found that planning and situational awareness did not keep the system secure.
regional-contingency-limits.strongerAI: Faster and more correlated automated dispatch could shrink intervention time. More capable forecasting might also help. Reassess joint physical margins.

reinforcement.proposal: Test correlated commands against independent regional constraints.
reinforcement.test: Demonstrate safe joint execution with realistic external contingencies.

available-power-restoration.title: Restoration
available-power-restoration.conditionBasis: The observed restoration reached affected load, using available recovery power. This is a bounded result.
available-power-restoration.strongerAI: Broader correlated disruption could remove the neighboring supply this recovery used. Better restoration planning could improve the response.

reinforcement.proposal: Validate recovery when usual external power is unavailable.
reinforcement.test: Restore representative essential loads with a missing recovery source and confirm duration.

tentative.question: Would recovery still work if neighboring grids also lost power?
tentative.basis: Restoration used supplies that remained energized. Affected entities did not need black starts.
tentative.unresolved: This recovery did not test what would happen after a wider shared failure, including one involving related AI systems. Testing that possibility would require showing that independent restoration resources can still supply affected loads.

NE-2003.title: Northeast blackout · 2003
NE-2003.observed: Monitoring and operational safeguards did not contain a regional disturbance.
NE-2003.notEstablished: AI did not cause this event. It does not establish the hypothetical route from shared AI models to a public-health catastrophe.
NE-2003.limit: This historical case concerns the physical grid and its human control structure.

operator-state-awareness.title: Monitoring and fallback
operator-state-awareness.result: Awareness failed when it was needed.
operator-state-awareness.conditionBasis: The task force identified monitoring and backup-tool failures in the incident.
operator-state-awareness.strongerAI: Faster automated actions increase the cost of stale feedback. More capable diagnosis may help only if its observations and fallback remain independent.

reinforcement.proposal: Use explicit loss-of-awareness triggers and independent fallback.
reinforcement.test: Demonstrate timely corrective action after a monitoring outage.

tentative.question: Could related AI dispatch tools turn a shared blind spot into a common error?
tentative.basis: The investigation identified failures of monitoring, situational awareness, and coordination.
tentative.unresolved: AI did not cause this event. Testing this possibility would require showing that related models share a consequential error and that independent dispatch checks fail to stop it.

presentation.fidelity: Non-AI incidents inform selected control mechanisms. Observed recovery is displayed alongside failure, and the public-health continuation remains conditional.
presentation.brittleness: Observed condition describes what the barrier did in this setting. Brittleness asks which changed dependency, capability, or operating condition would make it fail. A strengthened barrier can still be brittle. A single success does not establish robustness.

context.title: System setting

It includes model procurement, dispatch authorization, physical protection, regional coordination, and restoration. Essential services enter the analysis through their dependence on electricity and backup capacity.

targets.text: A regional grid uses related AI forecasts or control recommendations.

targets.text: Physical protection and regional coordination surround dispatch decisions.

cloud.summary: Grid interdependence constrains what operators can isolate and which supplies remain available for restoration. Related models may introduce shared errors.

controlEvidence.title: What kept a blackout from lasting longer?
controlEvidence.text: Inspect the available-power restoration barrier and its dependencies.
controlEvidence.limit: An effective response in one physical setting does not demonstrate robustness to correlated AI-driven disturbance.

questions.title: What worked?
questions.text: Separate the failed prevention from the response that restored supply.

questions.title: What did it depend on?
questions.text: Identify power sources, coordination, and essential-load access.

questions.title: Would stronger AI change it?
questions.text: Test correlated regional disruption as well as possible forecasting and restoration benefits.
